name: Ibn Zurayq al-Baghdadi
bio: Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Zurayq al-Katib al-Baghdadi was a poet of Baghdad who travelled to al-Andalus and died there; the editor Mahmud al-Tanahi found no biography that fixes his birth or death, and Brockelmann puts his death at about 420 AH (1029 CE). He is known for a single poem, his Ayniyya, “Do not blame him”, and al-Humaydi quotes Ibn Hazm: “It is said that whoever wears a carnelian ring, reads the Quran as Abu Amr read it, studies law in the school of al-Shafi'i and knows the poem of Ibn Zurayq by heart has perfected his refinement.” Al-Safadi also preserves an elegy of his for a rooster. Al-Sarraj, in Masari' al-Ushshaq, tells of a man from Baghdad who travelled to Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Andalusi, was given only a meagre gift, fell ill and died in the inn where he lodged, and was found with a sheet at his head bearing lines of this poem.
